keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 617-621 for a state Cliopatria lacks: 'the modern Hebei region' (infobox 'Hebei'), by late 619 'his territory north of the Yellow River and east of the Taihang Mountains', with fighting in Henan and Shandong. The page gives no area; the shape is the Hebei region without Gao Kaidao's strip (his Yan lay 'in the extreme northern Hebei region', Transition page). The extent in 617-618 was probably smaller; the page does not say.

region.text: Hebei north of the Yellow River and east of the Taihang, without Gao Kaidao's northern strip

ledger.note: 617: Dou Jiande becomes Prince of Changle. Spring 617; he had been a rebel commander since 616 after joining Gao Shida's bandits (infobox reign from 15 February 617). The Transition page dates the Xia 'c. 617-621' and says he 'further consolidated his holdings north of the Yellow River'.
618: Dou takes the title Prince of Xia. In winter 618 he is made Prince of Xia and changes the era name to Wufeng; the state is the Xia from here on. His capital is Leshou (Cangzhou).
619: the capital moves from Leshou to Ming Prefecture (modern Handan, Hebei).

619: Dou takes Liyang. In winter 619 he 'captured Liyang (modern Hebi, Henan)' together with Li Shentong, Li Gai, Wei Zheng and Princess Tong'an, who had been in Tang hands; the page does not name the previous holder.

region.text: Hebei north of the Yellow River and east of the Taihang, without Gao Kaidao's northern strip

ledger.note: 621: Li Shimin captures Dou Jiande at Hulao. 'In summer 621, Li Shimin defeated Dou at Hulao, where Dou was wounded and captured'; Emperor Gaozu 'publicly executed Dou' (infobox reign ends 28 May 621). The Xia ends; Liu Heita revives it in 621 until spring 623.

wars.name: Tang campaign against Dou Jiande and Wang Shichong

zones.text: Hulao, where Dou marched to relieve Wang Shichong's Luoyang

wars.outcome: Tang victory at Hulao in summer 621: Dou captured, Wang surrendered, the Xia and the Zheng annexed.
wars.note: Li Shimin besieged Luoyang from fall 620 (Wang Shichong page); in 619 Dou had made peace with Wang and cut relations when Wang took the throne from Yang Tong.

certainty.note: The page gives provinces and a mountain range (north of the Yellow River, east of the Taihang), not a boundary; the Henan and Shandong fighting fronts are not mapped.

notes: REBEL STATE written for a Sui rival Cliopatria lacks; wikipedia is the person's article (no state article). Start 617: the Xia name dates from winter 618. The infobox gives the end as 28 May 621 while the narrative has Hulao in summer 621. The land is the Hebei region read from the page's province span; the 617-618 extent and the Henan and Shandong fronts are unmapped. The Tang dossier (ea-04) names this regime 'Dou Jiande (Xia)' in its text; use the slug dou-jiande-s-xia. Counterparts needing dossiers: Liu Heita's Handong (621-623, former Xia territory); Gao Kaidao is a Cliopatria row (gao-kaidao, ea-04).
